item.title: [general] How AI Assistants are Moving the Security Goalposts
item.description: AI-based assistants or "agents" -- autonomous programs that have access to the user's computer, files, online services and can automate virtually any task -- are growing in popularity with developers and IT workers. item.title: [threat-intel] Who is the Kimwolf Botmaster “Dort”?
item.description: In early January 2026, KrebsOnSecurity revealed how a security researcher disclosed a vulnerability that was used to assemble Kimwolf, the world's largest and most disruptive botnet. Since then, the person in control of Kimwolf -- who goes by the handle "Dort" -- has coordinated a barrage of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS), doxing and email flooding attacks against the researcher and this author, and more recently caused a SWAT team to be sent to the researcher's home. This post examines what is knowable about Dort based on public information.

item.title: [malware] ‘Starkiller’ Phishing Service Proxies Real Login Pages, MFA
item.description: Most phishing websites are little more than static copies of login pages for popular online destinations, and they are often quickly taken down by anti-abuse activists and security firms. But a stealthy new phishing-as-a-service offering lets customers sidestep both of these pitfalls: It uses cleverly disguised links to load the target brand's real website, and then acts as a relay between the target and the legitimate site -- forwarding the victim's username, password and multi-factor authentication (MFA) code to the legitimate site and returning its responses.

item.title: [malware] Kimwolf Botnet Swamps Anonymity Network I2P

item.title: [vulnerability] Apple counters ClickFix attacks with macOS Terminal warning
item.description: <p>Apple has added a new security feature in macOS Tahoe 26.4 that warns users before they enter commands in Terminal that could cause harm. The goal is to stop ClickFix attacks, a social engineering trick that gets users to run malicious commands themselves. According to ESET, ClickFix activity jumped by more than 500% in the first half of 2025, making it the second-most common attack vector after phishing. The ClickFix tactic takes its name from &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/03/31/apple-macos-clickfix-attacks-terminal-warning/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/03/31/apple-macos-clickfix-attacks-terminal-warning/">Apple counters ClickFix attacks with macOS Terminal warning</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>

item.title: [malware] Axios npm packages backdoored in supply chain attack
item.description: <p>An unknown attacker has compromised the GitHub and npm accounts of the main developer of Axios, a widely used HTTP client library, and published npm packages backdoored with a malicious dependency that triggered the installation of droppers and remote access trojans. How the attack unfolded On March 30, 2026, with an account using a separate throwaway ProtonMail address, the attacker published on NPM a trojanized copy of the popular crypto-js JavaScript library of crypto standards. &#8230; <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/03/31/axios-npm-backdoored-supply-chain-attack/" rel="nofollow">More <span class="meta-nav">&#8594;</span></a></p> <p>The post <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/03/31/axios-npm-backdoored-supply-chain-attack/">Axios npm packages backdoored in supply chain attack</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.helpnetsecurity.com">Help Net Security</a>.</p>

item.title: [general] Inventors of Quantum Cryptography Win Turing Award
[general] Apple’s Camera Indicator Lights
item.description: <p>A <a href="https://daringfireball.net/2026/03/apple_enclaves_neo_camera_indicator">thoughtful review</a> of Apple&#8217;s system to alert users that the camera is on. It&#8217;s really well-designed, and important in a world where malware could surreptitiously start recording.</p> <blockquote><p>The reason it&#8217;s tempting to think that a dedicated camera indicator light is more secure than an on-display indicator is the fact that hardware is generally more secure than software, because it&#8217;s harder to tamper with. With hardware, a dedicated hardware indicator light can be connected to the camera hardware such that if the camera is accessed, the light must turn on, with no way for software running on the device, no matter its privileges, to change that. With an indicator light that is rendered on the display, it&#8217;s not foolish to worry that malicious software, with sufficient privileges, could draw over the pixels on the display where the camera indicator is rendered, disguising that the camera is in use...</p></blockquote>

item.title: [general] As the US Midterms Approach, AI Is Going to Emerge as a Key Issue Concerning Voters
item.description: <p>In December, the Trump administration signed an executive order that <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/11/technology/ai-trump-executive-order.html">neutered</a> states&#8217; ability to regulate AI by ordering his administration to both sue and withhold funds from states that try to do so. This action pointedly supported <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/08/us/politics/trump-executive-order-ai-laws.html">industry lobbyists</a> keen to avoid any constraints and consequences on their deployment of AI, while undermining the efforts of consumers, advocates, and industry associations concerned about AI&#8217;s harms who have spent years pushing for state regulation.</p> <p>Trump&#8217;s actions have clarified the ideological alignments around AI within America&#8217;s electoral factions. They set down lines on a new playing field for the midterm elections, prompting members of his party, the opposition, and all of us to consider where we stand in the debate over how and where to let AI transform our lives...</p>
